originalTitle: California tightens rules on AI data center energy and water use

content: California Gov. Gavin Newsom has signed seven bills designed to prevent AI data centers from passing utility costs onto residents, as reported earlier by the Los Angeles Times. The package of laws requires the California Public Utilities Commission to introduce a new rate classification for data centers while forcing them to pay for upgrades to local power grids and water systems. Other bills included in the package will require proposed data centers to disclose their estimated water use to local governments, along with information about energy efficiency and drought planning. They must also meet certain energy, water, and fuel consumption requirements before qualifying for a streamlined approval process. Last week, Newsom signed an executive order to speed up the creation of an AI “kill switch.” “While the Trump administration moves toward deregulation, communities are left to deal with the consequences — higher electricity demand, grid constraints, water use, and pollution,” Newsom says in the press release. “With these laws, we are ensuring that Californians remain in the driver’s seat — and that those profiting from data centers aren’t doing so at our expense.”

chineseContent: 据《洛杉矶时报》早些时候报道，加利福尼亚州州长加文·纽瑟姆签署了七项法案，旨在防止人工智能数据中心将公用事业成本转嫁给居民。该一揽子法律要求加州公用事业委员会为数据中心引入新的费率分类，同时迫使它们支付当地电网和供水系统的升级费用。该计划中包含的其他法案将要求拟议的数据中心向地方政府披露其估计的用水量，以及有关能源效率和干旱规划的信息。他们还必须满足某些能源、水和燃料消耗要求，才有资格获得简化的审批流程。上周，纽瑟姆签署了一项行政命令，以加快创建人工智能“终止开关”。纽瑟姆在新闻稿中表示：“虽然特朗普政府走向放松管制，但社区仍要应对由此带来的后果——电力需求增加、电网限制、用水和污染。” “通过这些法律，我们可以确保加州人继续掌握主导权，并且那些从数据中心获利的人不会以我们为代价。”
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于 AI 与科技趋势信号，适合用于观察工具选型、产品机会、开发者关注点和技术路线变化。
